The Kochi inspection market

Kochi (Cochin) hosts the BPCL Kochi Refinery (one of India's largest), Cochin Shipyard (India's largest public-sector shipyard — building the indigenous aircraft carrier INS Vikrant and commercial vessels), and the FACT (Fertilisers & Chemicals Travancore) complex. Shipbuilding, refining and offshore-tie-back inspection feed NDT demand.

Certifications most in demand in Kochi

Primary: ASNT. Secondary: ISNT. Also frequently requested: ISO 9712, PCN.

What drives NDT training demand in Kochi

Kochi carries BPCL's expanded refinery — among India's largest — Cochin Shipyard building and repairing up to carrier scale, the LNG terminal at Puthuvype, and a fabrication base serving all three. Every one of those assets is examined on intervals set by code, and the examinations must be performed by certified personnel — which is what creates continuous local demand for qualified technicians, and continuous pressure on employers to develop them.

Which methods to train first in this market

Training investment should follow the local work. In Kochi that means UT thickness and corrosion monitoring, phased array on welds, and API-track inspection knowledge; in the marine sector, UT thickness gauging at survey scale, MT on fatigue details, and visual survey discipline; and where fabrication work features, VT to CWI-style acceptance first, then UT and RT for coded work. A candidate who certifies against what local employers actually examine is employable months sooner than one who spreads across every method thinly.

Which certification scheme employers here expect

IBR governs statutory boilers and steam lines, classification societies rule the shipyard work, and both ISNT and ASNT certifications circulate; refinery shutdown windows concentrate the market's demand sharply.

For a candidate this decides the route before any course is booked: train toward the scheme your target employers name in their contracts. Where both employer-based (SNT-TC-1A) and central (ISO 9712 / PCN) certification circulate, the central certificate travels with you between employers — worth weighing against the faster employer-based route. How ASNT certification works · ISO 9712 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Levels, honestly explained

Level I performs calibrations and examinations under supervision — the entry point, usually reached in one method first. Level II sets up, interprets against the code and signs the report; it is the level contracts in Kochi actually specify. Level III writes and approves procedures and qualifies the Level I/IIs — the level a growing inspection function eventually needs to own or engage. Progression is training hours plus documented experience hours, so anyone already working under supervision moves faster than a cold start.
